sources.title: Leonardo da Vinci (1452–1519): A map of Imola
sources.locator: Collection item 912284, catalogue description paragraphs on the August 1502 appointment, autumn 1502 Imola context and map construction
intended_claims: Leonardo was appointed General Architect and Engineer to Cesare Borgia in August 1502
Cesare Borgia and his entourage were in Imola in autumn 1502
The catalogued map of Imola is associated with Leonardo's work in that context

sources.title: Leonardo da Vinci (1452–1519): A map of southern Tuscany
sources.locator: Collection item 912278, catalogue description paragraphs on Borgia service in 1502–1503, the June 1502 Arezzo context and the map's represented area
intended_claims: Leonardo was in Cesare Borgia's service in 1502–1503
The catalogued map represents a wide area of southern Tuscany
The map is associated by the catalogue with the June 1502 Arezzo context

sources.title: The Procession to Calvary
sources.locator: Catalogue note 21: October 1503 Battle of Anghiari commission and 4 May 1504 formal contract
intended_claims: Leonardo received the Battle of Anghiari commission in October 1503
The formal contract was made on 4 May 1504
The work context included the Sala del Papa at Santa Maria Novella

rights.attribution: The National Gallery, London, online scholarly catalogue, note 21

sources.title: Rocca Sforzesca di Imola
sources.locator: Historical overview paragraphs on the 1499 return to direct papal domination and Leonardo's 1502 consultation/visit evidenced by the Imola plan
intended_claims: Leonardo visited Imola in the 1502 fortress-consultation context
The plan of Imola is presented as evidence of that visit
The 1499 siege was followed by a return to direct papal domination

rights.attribution: Comune di Imola — Musei Civici, Rocca Sforzesca historical overview
